title: Practical quantization notes and onboarding checklist - Feb 27 2026
content:
Quick context: informal notes from the Feb 27 hands-on sync. Purpose is to capture recent microbench results for aggressive quantization (int8 / Q4_0 variants), the lightweight evals we ran, and a rough onboarding checklist for bringing a new open model through our serving pipeline. Mostly notes-to-self and action items for the next sprint.

Summary of experiments this week:
- Model: vicuna-13b-like fork (checkpoint A). Goal: test int8 static quant + KV cache behavior under 1k token sequences.
- Runtime: local dev machine (4xA100-sim), runtime branch: pr-873 (see linked PR).
- Configs tested: FP16 baseline; int8 static (symmetric) with per-channel scale; Q4_0 mix (activation clipping).

Key microbench numbers (median over 20 runs):
- FP16 baseline: 1.9ms/token (seq length 512, batch 1)
- int8 static: 2.2ms/token (+16% latency), memory down ~38%
- Q4_0 mix: 2.05ms/token (+8%), memory down ~48%
- KV cache penalty: int8 shows ~+5% token latency increase when KV grows > 32k entries (investigate memory access pattern)

Quality eval quick-pass (held-out prompt set: 1200 QA + 300 code gen examples):
- FP16 baseline: exact-match QA 78.4%, code-pass 63.2%
- int8 static: exact-match QA 75.1% (-3.3%), code-pass 60.8% (-2.4%)
- Q4_0 mix: exact-match QA 76.5% (-1.9%), code-pass 61.7% (-1.5%)
Notes: degradation concentrated on long-context multi-step math prompts. Short-chat and instruction tasks are mostly stable. We should flag worst-case prompts for rollback tests.

Observations: 
- int8 static is cheaper in mem but higher quantization noise on some arithmetic tokens. Suspect scale estimation; test per-row vs per-channel again.
- Q4_0 mix seems a good tradeoff for memory; small latency hit but better EE for code tasks.
- Batching: continuous batching reduced per-token cost by 12% for batched concurrent streams (batch size 4) but increased p95 latency — needs policy integration in router.

Onboarding checklist for a new open model (short actionable checklist):
1) Pull checkpoint into staging bucket + automated conversion script (TODO: add script to repo, owner Omar).
2) Run quantization recipe (per-channel int8 + calibration on 2k prompts). Save calibration artifacts.
3) Run microbench harness: latency, mem, KV stress, streaming tests. Attach perf artifacts to PR.
4) Run quick eval suite (QA/code/long-context) and compare to baseline. Flag delta >2% on major metrics.
5) Sanity integration test with canary routing (1% traffic, auto-fallback to baseline on errors/timeouts).
6) Docs: add model card + known failure modes to Confluence page.

Owners and near-term action items:
- Omar Patel: add conversion + quant script to infra repo (due Mar 10).
- Leah Kim: expand quick eval suites with focused long-context math prompts (due Mar 5).
- Marcus Li: investigate KV cache memory access pattern and propose kernel-level optimization (due Mar 12).
- Hannah Chen (me): write rollout canary config template and PR to product (due Mar 8).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Threshold for acceptable QA delta: currently proposal is 2% absolute on exact-match. Is that too strict for some customer classes? (raise at triage).
- Should we prefer Q4_0 mix as default quant profile for new models, given memory wins and smaller accuracy hit? Tradeoff with latencies for low-SLO customers.
- Should we capture calibration dataset snapshots to reproduce regressions exactly? Storage cost vs reproducibility tradeoff.

Random notes / quick ideas:
- Add a small eval that measures numeric stability (synthetic arithmetic ladder) to quickly detect quantization regressions.
- Consider running a small A/B with synthetic high-KV loads to ensure we detect KV blowups early.

References / links (also in metadata):
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/873 (batching + quant hooks)
- Jira: ML-771 (quantization pipeline), ENG-1423 (canary routing feature request)
- Confluence: Applied-ML/quantization-playbook (working draft)

Meeting cadence notes:
- Keep hands-on sync weekly on Fridays 10:30am PT. Use the Friday slot for 'bring one failing prompt' exercise.

Status: draft. Will convert to in_review once PRs are merged and we have reproducible calibration artifacts attached.

Notes-to-self: remember to add an example of model-card 'known failures' for arithmetic tokens and link to the small arithmetic ladder test.

-- end of notes --
